mintAuthority.summary: FRAX native issuance is Ethereum-only and includes six currently authorized pools/AMOs. The token and main AMO Minter are direct contracts, but the authorized Convex AMO is a transparent proxy controlled by the Frax Comptroller 3-of-5 Safe. Satellite deployments remain bridge representations.

sources.label: Authorized Convex AMO transparent proxy verified source

controls.label: FRAX AMO Minter
controls.capDescription: At block 26095801, mintFraxForAMO enforces the 700,000,000 FRAX aggregate cap and restricts destinations to approved AMOs. The separate oldPoolRedeem path mints to the minter itself under collateral-borrow checks rather than frax_mint_cap, but a pinned simulation reverted because legacy-pool redemption is paused. Owner or timelock governance can change the cap; the 700 million figure is not a whole-contract bound independent of these other controls.
controls.evidence: At Ethereum block 26095801, owner() returned Frax Comptroller Safe 0xb1748c79709f4ba2dd82834b8c82d4a505003f27, timelock_address() returned 0x8412ebf45bac1b340bbe8f318b928c466c4e39ca, and frax_mint_cap() returned 700,000,000 FRAX. The cap is unchanged from the 2026-08-08 review and remains raiseable by owner or timelock. This is one of six authorized native pools/AMOs, not the entire native issuance surface.

controls.label: Frax Comptroller Safe
controls.evidence: At Ethereum block 26095801, pinned getOwners()/getThreshold() reads confirmed the listed 3-of-5 owners; getModulesPaginated returned no enabled modules. Guard and module-guard storage slots were zero, and the fallback handler matched the prior observation. The AMO Minter owner and the Convex AMO ProxyAdmin owner both resolved to this Safe. The Safe retains an immediate owner path to authorize AMOs, raise the main 700 million FRAX cap, and upgrade an authorized native-mint proxy; the separate FRAX timelock delay() returned 172800 seconds.

review.evidence: Re-reviewed at Ethereum block 26095801. Enumeration of frax_pools_array indices 0-24, terminated by an out-of-bounds revert at index 25, found six nonzero native pool/AMO addresses; frax_pools(address) independently confirmed the five previously omitted entries. The main AMO Minter has a 700 million FRAX cap on mintFraxForAMO and a Frax Comptroller 3-of-5 Safe owner. Rari and UniV3 mintFRAXForInvestments have separate 100 million and 12.5 million FRAX caps. The main minter's oldPoolRedeem and UniV3's mintRedeemPart1 instead use collateral-borrow checks; both pinned simulations reverted because legacy-pool redemption is paused. These observations do not establish a whole-contract FRAX cap independent of the other control paths. Pool_USDC is mint-paused but retains token-level authorization. The authorized Convex AMO is a transparent proxy with implementation 0x485395dad57afac9e926e634a25dba5c3708e25d and ProxyAdmin 0xe53d45abe10ce20427d20c5a1b6360fa5ba0ce0a owned by the same Safe; the earlier profile's immutable whole-issuance conclusion omitted this path. Canonical FRAX and the main AMO Minter themselves have zero implementation and correct admin slots and direct verified sources. Historical 2026-08-15 economic posture remains: raiseable owner-path caps are economically unbounded; the issuer balance sheet self-reports whole-supply liabilities continuously; supervision is none. The independently fetched 2026-10-01T07:43:47Z balance sheet reports totalAssets, totalLiabilities, remaining FRAX supply, borrowed debt and FXB adjustments, but self-published accounting is not independent assurance. No incident finding is inferred from these additional authorized contracts.
